Module np.cincuentazo
Package np.cincuentazo.view

Class GameView

java.lang.Object
np.cincuentazo.view.GameView
public class GameView extends Object
Pure-rendering utility class for the main game screen.

All methods are static: GameView owns no state of its own and never mutates the model. Its single responsibility is to translate a snapshot of model objects (Card, Player) into JavaFX nodes, applying the correct CSS classes and event handlers. If how the game looks changes, this is the only class that needs to change.

Why static methods instead of an instance?

GameController is the FXML controller, so it is the only class allowed to receive @FXML-injected nodes â€” JavaFX requires that. Rather than wiring a separate instance and passing every node through a constructor, static helpers accept the nodes as parameters on each call. This avoids a 12-parameter constructor while keeping rendering logic out of the controller.

SRP note

Before this class was introduced, every rendering method lived inside GameController, mixed with event handling, turn orchestration, and scene navigation. Extracting these methods gives each class exactly one reason to change.

  • Method Details

    • renderTableCard

      public static void renderTableCard(javafx.scene.layout.StackPane tablePile, javafx.scene.control.Label lblLastCard, Card topCard)
      Updates the table pile display and the last-card text label.

      Removes all card views previously added to tablePile (keeping the background Pane at index 0 intact), then adds a new CardView for topCard if one exists.

      Parameters:
      tablePile - the StackPane that renders the top of the table stack; must have at least one child (the background)
      lblLastCard - label that shows a text description of the top card
      topCard - the card currently on top of the table pile, or null if the table is empty

    • renderHumanHand

      public static void renderHumanHand(javafx.scene.layout.HBox humanHand, List<Card> cards, boolean isHumanTurn, int tableSum, IntFunction<javafx.event.EventHandler<javafx.scene.input.MouseEvent>> clickHandlerFactory)
      Rebuilds the human player's hand in the UI.

      For each card in cards:

      • A CardView is created face-up.
      • If it is not the human's turn, or if the card is not legally playable at the current table sum, the card is visually disabled (CardView.setCardDisabled(boolean)).
      • If it is the human's turn and the card is playable, a hover animation and a click handler (supplied by clickHandlerFactory) are attached.
      Parameters:
      humanHand - the HBox that holds the human's card views; cleared before repopulating
      cards - the ordered list of cards in the human's hand
      isHumanTurn - true when the human must play a card (i.e., it is their turn AND they have not yet drawn their replacement card this turn)
      tableSum - the current running sum on the table; used to determine which cards are legally playable
      clickHandlerFactory - a factory that, given a card's 0-based hand index, returns the EventHandler to attach to that card's view on click

    • renderMachineHand

      public static void renderMachineHand(javafx.scene.layout.HBox handBox, javafx.scene.control.Label countLabel, int handSize, Function<Integer,Card> cardProvider)
      Rebuilds one machine player's hand display with face-down card backs.

      Clears handBox and adds one CardView per card, rendered face-down so the human cannot see the machine's cards. Also updates countLabel with the current hand size.

      Parameters:
      handBox - the HBox that holds this machine's card views; cleared before repopulating
      countLabel - label that shows the number of cards in this machine's hand
      handSize - number of cards currently in the machine's hand
      cardProvider - a function that returns the card at a given 0-based hand index; used to create each CardView

    • updateStatusBadge

      public static void updateStatusBadge(javafx.scene.control.Label label, Player player, Player current)
      Updates a player's status badge label with the appropriate CSS class and display text.

      Exactly one of the following CSS classes is active at any time:

      • badge-eliminated â€” player has been knocked out.
      • badge-active â€” it is currently this player's turn.
      • badge-waiting â€” player is alive but waiting for their turn.
      All three classes are removed before the new one is added to avoid accumulation.
      Parameters:
      label - the badge Label node to update
      player - the player this badge represents
      current - the player whose turn it is right now

    • addEliminatedLogEntry

      public static void addEliminatedLogEntry(javafx.scene.layout.VBox elimList, String playerName)
      Appends one entry to the elimination log panel (HU-5).

      Creates a new Label with the CSS class elim-entry and adds it to the bottom of elimList. Called once per eliminated player, in the order they were knocked out.

      Parameters:
      elimList - the VBox that acts as the elimination log container
      playerName - display name of the eliminated player
